blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 56 in June to 59 in October (+5.4%), and it took 14.2% of the city’s 247 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 17 in June to 10 in October (−41.2%), and it took 7.8% of the city’s 230 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Albion for detached houses in October (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in July, August (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, August, September, October (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in July (a buyers’ best bet).

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default form: Houses sit under the compact urban zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, with RS-1 (Single Detached Residential), s. 605 — minimum lot area 668.0 m², minimum lot width 18.0 m, minimum lot depth 27.0 m, maximum lot coverage 40% — as the standard urban house zone in the bylaw's schedule. The Area Plan's residential designations include Low Density Residential (single detached at an urban standard, with lot sizes at 2,000 m² in the designation text read), Ground-Oriented Residential, Cluster Residential and Townhouse, plus an Albion Village Commercial node — plan designations, stated only as the plan text states them, never as a for-sale lot inventory.
Bare-land strata: none verified: The four strata townhome complexes below are built strata on built lots, not bare-land strata, and must never be presented as lot stock.
Rydge is a cross-reference only and is not counted as part of Albion. Sources classify it differently, so a buyer searching under only one name will mix the two areas' stock.

Assemblies / development sites — documented as plans, never as inventory: Council adopted updates to the Albion Area Plan on October 28, 2025 — responding to regional-partner feedback, enhancing walking and cycling connections, supporting the growth of local commercial nodes, and introducing buffers where urban development meets farmland; the plan seeks a balance between new residential development and protection of environmentally sensitive areas across a range of housing styles. Check a lot's current designation before valuing it as a plain house lot; a designation is not an approval and no development site is listed as inventory here.
Tenure records — never lot stock, stated with the reason: Park/co-op official confirmation of rules, rents and counts: Not confirmed.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Albion

items.t: Municipality: City of Maple Ridge, BC.
Boundaries: the City publishes no boundary for the MLS sub-area as such: Not verified as an official boundary. The Albion Area Plan's Schedule 1 map is the closest official boundary document.

Nearby areas: Cottonwood and East Central to the west along Lougheed Highway, Thornhill to the northeast, Kanaka Creek / North Maple Ridge ground to the north, and the Fraser River along the south edge.

Main roads and commute: Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) along the south side; 240 Street is the main north–south road; 102 Avenue and 104 Avenue run east–west through the residential area; the Golden Ears Bridge west of the city connects Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows to Langley and Surrey.

Transit: Haney Place Exchange is in the Town Centre to the west (routes include the R3, 701, 733, 741, 743, 744, 745, 746, 748, 749 and 791; the R3 runs Coquitlam Central Station to Haney Place). Port Haney Station (22300 River Road) and Maple Meadows Station (20010 Dunn Avenue) serve the west side of the city; West Coast Express trains run weekdays between Waterfront and Mission City.

Schools physically in the area (Ministry-listed names and addresses only): Albion Elementary, 10031 240 Street; c'usqunela Elementary, 24093 104 Avenue; Kanaka Creek Elementary, 11120 234a Street (at the area's west edge); Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary, 10445 245 Street. SD42 has no middle tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12).

Kanaka Creek Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) runs along the area's west side, with the Canyon Trail to Cliff Falls and the Bell-Irving Hatchery. No library branch sits in Albion — Maple Ridge Public Library is at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road in the Town Centre. Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, is the community hospital with 24/7 emergency care; the Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 121 – 11900 Haney Place, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Albion

items.t: OCP citation contested — flagged, resolved nowhere; Albion Area Plan settled: The settled part: the Albion Area Plan is Chapter 10.2 of the OCP, and Council adopted updates to it on October 28, 2025 (walking/cycling connections, local commercial nodes, farmland buffers). Quote the OCP bylaw number only from a current City document for the specific property.

Floodplain (south edge): the south edge of Albion sits along the Fraser River and Kanaka Creek — the flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic (including freeboard), a covenant on title identifies construction in the floodplain, no habitable floor space may be located below the flood construction level on affected lots, and Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h) prohibits rental accommodation (suites) on floodplain properties.

ALR block — full form (South Albion ground): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)). Residence caps: one principal residence per parcel, maximum 500 m²; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Farm class (BC Assessment) in full three-tier form: $2,500 of gross farm income at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha above that; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — applications by October 31. A flat "$2,500+" line is an error and none is asserted here.

BC strata block — applies in full to any strata lot here (including the four townhome complexes' resales): Form B (SPA s. 59), provided within 7 days, max $35 plus up to 25¢/page; depreciation reports every five years for stratas with five or more lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 and Regulation 7.01, May 1, 2023 exemptions); a "45+" listing line is not a valid age bylaw. None of Albion's four complexes carries a verified 55+ bylaw — Albion verifies zero 55+ stock, and Maple Ridge has zero verified 55+ strata townhouses. For The Warwick, first establish whether the unit is a developer sale or a resale, because the document route (REDMA/GST vs Form B) differs.

Presales (REDMA) — Warwick units only: REDMA s. 21 gives a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging the disclosure statement, with deposits in trust under s. 18 — the frame for any unit still on a developer contract at The Warwick.

Planned transit — price on today's service: TransLink's Langley–Haney Place BRT is in detailed planning — 22 km between Willowbrook and Haney Place with peak service every 10 minutes; designs, costs and timelines are not yet determined.

blocks.text: Good to know about Albion

items.t: All four townhome complexes stand within a few blocks of one corner. Albion Station, Ridgemont, Spencer Brook Estates and The Warwick all cluster at 104 Avenue / 240 Street, beside the Albion Commercial Corner and c'usqunela Elementary — complex-level comparables here are effectively a single-intersection market, and none of it is lot stock.
Spencer Brook Estates (EPS763, 40 homes, built 2015) was verified by the 55-plus run — while proving it was not 55+ — and never appeared in the condos run's three-complex townhome list.

The farmland buffer is new policy with a date. The Oct 28, 2025 Area Plan update introduced buffers where urban development meets farmland — houses closest to the South Albion ALR edge now sit beside a stated buffer policy, not just a field. Whether that edge discounts or complicates those houses is Jared's Section 8 question, not verified here.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Albion

items.t: Zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019: Houses sit under the compact urban zones of the bylaw, with RS-1 (Single Detached Residential), s. Verify a specific parcel's exact zone with the City before pricing any use.

Suites and SSMUH (urban ground): one secondary suite per lot inside the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not within the floodplain area; eligible single-detached and duplex lots may have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws. On ALR land the ALC suite rule above (inside the principal residence only) controls instead — the two regimes meet at the South Albion line and must not be mixed.

Floodplain — the south edge: the south edge of Albion sits along the Fraser River and Kanaka Creek — the flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic (including freeboard), a covenant on title identifies construction in the floodplain, no habitable floor space may be located below the flood construction level on affected lots, and Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h) prohibits rental accommodation (suites) on floodplain properties.

blocks.text: Good to know about Albion

items.t: Albion's plan now buffers the farm line instead of erasing it: The October 28, 2025 Area Plan update is the rare growth-area update that adds protection at the edge: buffers where urban development meets farmland, alongside commercial-node growth and walking / cycling links. For a house lot beside South Albion farmland, that buffer policy is part of what the lot will live next to — read the designation, not just the house.

The Rydge seam cuts the other way from most classification fights: Here the developer claims the growth-area name (Albion) and the board claims the hillside name (Thornhill MR) — the reverse of the usual marketing direction.

Albion: streets and boundaries

items.t: Albion is the east Maple Ridge growth area around 240 Street and Lougheed Highway, listed by the City as "Albion/Kanaka."

The Albion Area Plan, Chapter 10.2 of the Official Community Plan (OCP), is the closest official boundary document, including the North East Albion area and the Albion Flats next to Lougheed Highway and 240 Street.
240 Street runs north-south, 102 Avenue and 104 Avenue run east-west through the housing, and the Fraser River forms the south edge.
Kanaka Creek runs along the west side, with Cottonwood and East Central to the west and Thornhill to the northeast.

blocks.text: Albion: the housing stock

items.t: Albion's housing is newer detached houses plus ground-oriented and townhouse product, matching the plan's own designation mix.
The industrial lands sit in the Albion Flats by Lougheed Highway, separate from the residential corridors on 102 Avenue and 104 Avenue.

items.t: The 2025 update enhances walking and cycling connections and consolidates land-use policies to reflect provincial housing legislation.

blocks.text: Albion: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Albion Community Centre at 24165 104 Avenue is co-located with c'usqunela Elementary at 104 Avenue and 240 Street, and opened June 22, 2022.
The centre replaced the historic Albion Hall on 240 Street, built by volunteers in 1923 and demolished after a 2010 inspection found it at end of life.
Kanaka Creek Regional Park runs 400 hectares along 12 kilometres of Kanaka Creek, with the Canyon Trail to Cliff Falls and the Bell-Irving Hatchery.
The Albion Fairgrounds and Albion Sports Complex at 23778 104 Avenue host Planet Ice and the Golden Ears Winter Club curling rink.
Route 748 loops Haney Place via Lougheed Highway, River Road, 240 Street and 100 Avenue through Thornhill and Albion streets.

blocks.text: Albion: development and new projects

items.t: Albion Community Centre, 24165 104 Avenue — City facility, completed, grand opening June 22, 2022, co-located with c'usqunela Elementary (status read November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Albion: getting around

items.t: No West Coast Express station sits in Albion; Port Haney Station at 22300 River Road and Maple Meadows Station serve the city from the west side.
Route 748 is the Albion loop bus to Haney Place, via 240 Street and 100 Avenue.
The Golden Ears Bridge, west of Albion, replaced the Albion Ferry in 2009 and is now the Fraser River crossing to Langley and Surrey.

blocks.text: Albion: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check floodplain status and the title covenant for any lot near the Fraser River or Kanaka Creek, using the City's floodplain construction guide and maps.
Check ALR status parcel by parcel for South Albion lots at the farmland edge, where the 2025 plan adds urban-farmland buffers.
Kanaka Creek is a riparian corridor, so lots backing onto the creek need a development-permit and tree check the plan map alone does not settle.
